coachingPoints: Rip it LOW — the ball travels under the defender's reaching arm, not over it.
Rip with force; a slow rip gets deflected by the defender's hands.
Keep your pivot foot planted through the entire rip — lifting it is a travel.
The first dribble must be hard and past the defender's hip — a soft dribble lets them recover.
Use it when the defender reaches or crowds you, not when they give you space.
commonMistakes: Ripping the ball up high into the defender's chest — that's a charge or a strip.
Starting the dribble before the rip — the defender just takes the ball.
Losing the pivot foot in the excitement — travels kill the best rip-throughs.
Ripping when there's no pressure — if the defender is sagging, just drive.
description: Rip the ball low and hard across your body past a reaching defender — the aggressive counter to pressure.
gameSituations: Catching on the wing with a defender crowding you — rip through and go.
Against a defender who reaches on the catch — their arm is the trigger.
Baseline catches where the defender overplays the middle — rip baseline and drive.

howTo.detail: Catch in triple threat with a defender pressuring you — hands active, body close. Your pivot foot is set.
howTo.title: Catch under pressure

howTo.detail: In one violent motion, swing the ball low and hard across your body — from one hip to the other — keeping it below the defender's reaching hands. This is the 'rip.'
howTo.title: Rip low across your body

howTo.detail: As the ball crosses, your pivot foot stays planted and your free foot steps past the defender's hip. Your shoulder should brush their chest — you're going through the gap they left.
howTo.title: Step through the gap

howTo.detail: The instant the ball passes your body, bounce it hard — one aggressive dribble past the defender's lead foot. Now you're driving with the defender sealed behind you.
howTo.title: First dribble past the hip

title: Rip Through
whatIsIt: The rip through is an aggressive move from triple threat: you swing the ball low and hard across your body, past a pressuring defender, and drive. It turns defensive pressure into your advantage.

When a defender crowds you or reaches for the ball, the rip through punishes them — the ball goes under their arm while your body goes through the gap. It's a power move, not a finesse move, and it sets the tone for the drive.
whyItMatters: Defenders who pressure the catch want you to pick up the ball or panic. The rip through does neither — it attacks the pressure itself. Players who rip through confidently force defenders to back off, which opens up the entire triple-threat game: jab, shoot, and drive.
